transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Lee (HeliosGrid CTO), Priya Menon (Head of ML), Sam Ortiz (Platform Eng)
---
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we got 50 mi-ish booked, is that right?
[00:12] Dana: Yep that's us. Thanks for making time. Quick intro, I'm Dana, CTO at HeliosGrid, we do grid forecasting and fleet management for distributed solar.
[00:22] Priya: Hi, Priya, ML lead. We're evaluating options to put an LLM in front of ops triage and customer-facing summaries.
[00:28] Avery: Awesome. High level today — quickstart credits and time-to-first-token, plus Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fit. Marco will do infra and benchmark talk.
[00:37] Marco: Hey all. Quick note, I might say "V P C" or "K V cache" a bit weird from notes, transcription may glitch.
[00:44] Sam: No worries. Real question: we need to know how fast we can get first token and how predictable latency is under bursty loads.
[00:52] Avery: Totally. Quick question for qualification — what's your expected request pattern day one? QPS and typical prompt sizes?
[01:02] Priya: For MVP, 10-20 qps, average prompt 120-300 tokens. Some longer context up to 2k for troubleshooting sessions.
[01:12] Dana: Also data residency: EU-only processing for parts of the pipeline — we might need a VPC or private deployment.
[01:20] Marco: Cool, that maps to the three common paths. Hosted API is fastest to TTFT — we can provision credits and you can be calling in minutes. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools for predictable p95 throughput. Private is either VPC peering or on-prem for EU and air-gapped needs.
[01:36] Priya: When you say "minutes" for hosted, what is realistic? Ten minutes?
[01:41] Avery: From sign-up to token, if you use our PLG flow it's often under 30 minutes to first call. With our quickstart template and SDK snippets you'll do a sample generation in under an hour. Free credits help run the first few thousand tokens for evaluation.
[01:54] Sam: Ok. But TTFT under load — our concern is cold-start p95 when cache is cold.
[02:01] Marco: Right. Cold KV cache and kernel warmup can add latency. In hosted with our smart routing and prefix cache, p50 for short prompts hits sub-200ms typically on supported model variants, p95 may be 350-600ms depending on model and sequence. Dedicated can lower variance because we pin model variants to pools and reduce noisy neighbors.
[02:22] Dana: Are those numbers from your public benchmarks? We need concrete numbers for different payloads.
[02:28] Marco: We have telemetry and perf profiles, but for your workload we propose a short SE benchmark — run the same prompt set on hosted, a dedicated reservation profile, and a VPC-connected private deploy if you want. We usually do a 2-hour workshop.
[02:40] Priya: That sounds good. What about cost? Our CFO will push back if per-token is high for high QPS.
[02:47] Avery: Cost tradeoffs: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-token pricing and lower operational overhead; dedicated is reserved capacity with a commitment but reduced unit cost for heavy throughput. Private has higher baseline costs (infrastructure, license), but full isolation. We can model 3-month projections after the benchmark.
[03:03] Sam: For private, are we talking full on-prem, or a VPC peering setup into your control plane?
[03:08] Marco: Both options — VPC/private data plane keeps compute in your cloud and our control plane manages deployments, or fully private on-prem bundle. The VPC option still allows audit logs to flow into your S3 and KMS integration for keys.
[03:21] Dana: Security is a showstopper. We need SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, SSO via SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM support, and immutable audit logs.
[03:31] Avery: Yes, we have SOC2 and ISO artifacts, SAML SSO and RBAC, and integrations with major KMS vendors. We'll send the security pack after this call.
[03:38] Priya: Can you support key-per-customer so logs can't be read by a third party?
[03:42] Marco: With Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS you can keep keys. Hosted can integrate with a bring-your-own-key approach for certain enterprise plans. We'll include the details in the security doc.
[03:53] Dana: Great. On compliance, we need data retention controls and the ability to purge data tied to a customer id.
[03:59] Avery: We have API endpoints and retention policies that can be configured; for Private you have full control.
[04:05] Sam: For the SE benchmark, what artifacts should we prepare?
[04:09] Marco: Provide: (1) sample prompt set (50-100 prompts) covering short and long contexts, (2) expected concurrency pattern (burst vs steady), (3) success SLOs — p50/p95 targets and cost targets. We'll run hosted vs dedicated baseline.
[04:23] Priya: I'll pull together prompts — some forecasting requests, triage notes, and a few customer report templates.
[04:28] Dana: Timeline — we want a pilot in production-ish in 8–10 weeks if the numbers line up.
[04:34] Avery: That's realistic. Pilot plan: quickstart using PLG flow with credits for devs (week 1), SE benchmark (week 2), pilot reservation decision (weeks 3–4), pilot rollout (weeks 6–10).
[04:46] Sam: One more: observability. Do you expose token-level latency, cost breakdowns, tracing?
[04:52] Marco: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards, token-cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We'll give you a walkthrough in the benchmark session.
[04:59] Priya: Competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and an OpenAI integration. Anthropic's model latency is ok but total cost looked higher; OpenAI has scale but we want more predictable infra.
[05:12] Avery: Makes sense. We'll show where Redwood sits on predictability and cost controls.
[05:18] Dana: Any blockers on our side to try hosted quickstart now?
[05:22] Sam: Our security team will need the SOC2 artifacts and SAML SSO details. Until they sign off, they won't allow external keys in our production.
[05:30] Avery: We'll send the security pack and a sample SAML config. In parallel, we can provision dev credits and a sandbox account so your engineers can TTFT without touching production.
[05:40] Marco: For the sandbox benchmark we can also provide a small dedicated pool in the Redwood sandbox to simulate pinned GPUs — it won't be production but helps see variance.
[05:49] Dana: That would be helpful. Also EU residency: can the sandbox data be restricted to eu-west-1?
[05:55] Avery: Yes, we'll provision the sandbox in the eu region for that.
[05:59] Priya: About model variants — do you do quantized variants that trade quality for cost? We might be fine with slightly lower quality for cheaper inference on bulk ops.
[06:08] Marco: We recommend model/quantization profiles per workload. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization settings and batching configs. We'll include initial recommendations after the benchmark.
[06:17] Dana: Ok, recap: send security pack, enable sandbox credits in EU, schedule 2h benchmark, provide sample prompts. Anything else?
[06:25] Avery: Pricing. I'll include a tailored pricing sheet and a credits offer — probably a dev credits pool and an optional dedicated pilot quote.
[06:32] Sam: One practical: do you support IP allowlists and private link?
[06:36] Marco: We support allowlists, VPC peering, and private link patterns; details in the deployment docs.
[06:42] Dana: Sweet. Let's lock a time for the benchmark — next week works for us.
[06:47] Marco: I'll send a Doodle for two windows — Tue/Wed mid-day in your timezone.
[06:52] Avery: Great. Any final questions?
[06:55] Priya: None. Thanks.
[06:57] Dana: Thanks everyone.
[07:00] [Later section — deeper infra Q&A, transcription has occasional mislabels]
[07:05] Sam: If we go Dedicated, what's the minimum commit?
[07:09] Avery: Typical initial commitment is a month of reserved capacity; we can structure a 3-month pilot with reduced rates. Exact numbers in the quote.
[07:17] Priya: Does Dedicated allow you to pin models to a specific GPU family?
[07:22] Marco: Yes, we can pin to a family and even specific instance types to control latency and kernel choices. There are tradeoffs with cost and availability.
[07:31] Sam: For on-prem, what's the packaging?
[07:34] Marco: We ship a private appliance package — orchestration layer, runtime, and you provide hardware. It's heavier lift but full isolation.
[07:40] Dana: Good to know.
[07:42] Marco: Also want to note — some words may be mis-transcribed; e.g., "KV cache" could show as K V cache.
[07:49] Avery: Ok wrapping up — I'll send the security doc + pricing today or tomorrow, Marco will propose benchmark windows and we'll bake a sample prompt checklist for Priya.
[07:58] Dana: Thanks team.
[08:00] Meeting end.
